html:
Damascus is the capital of Syria and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It stands in an oasis watered by the Barada river, at the edge of the desert, where caravan routes met.

Around 1000 BCE it was the capital of Aram-Damascus, the strongest kingdom of the Arameans, until Assyria conquered it in 732 BCE. Persians, Greeks and Romans followed. In the New Testament, Paul was converted on the road to Damascus.

Arab Muslim armies took the city in 634. From 661 to 750 it was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate, which ruled from Spain to Central Asia. The caliph al-Walid built the Umayyad Mosque there in the early 700s on the site of a church. When the Abbasids moved the capital to Baghdad, Damascus became a provincial city, but it stayed a centre of learning, crafts and trade. Famous goods included Damascus steel and damask cloth. Saladin ruled from it and is buried there, and Timur sacked it in 1401.

Under the Ottomans from 1516 it was the gathering point of the great pilgrim caravan to Mecca, and the Hejaz Railway later followed that route. After French rule it became the capital of independent Syria in 1946. The Ba'ath Party was founded there in 1947.
sum: Damascus is the capital of Syria and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It stands in an oasis watered by the Barada river, at the edge of the desert, where caravan routes met.
